title: Login System
story: Your app needs a login function. When someone tries to sign in, three things can happen: they succeed (you need their username for a welcome message), the password is wrong, or the user doesn't exist. An enum with data captures all three outcomes.
why: Multiple failure modes with different meanings are perfectly captured by multiple error variants.
analogy: A login attempt is like knocking on a door. You either get welcomed in (Success with your name), told the key doesn't fit (WrongPassword), or told nobody lives there (UserNotFound).
try_it: Add a `LockedOut(remaining_minutes: Int)` variant for users who've tried too many times. Update `try_login` so that user "bob" always gets LockedOut with 15 minutes. Test all four possible outcomes.
tips: Check the user first, then the password — this prevents leaking whether a user exists (security best practice says check both anyway, but for learning, order logically)
Carry useful data in success variants (like username) so the caller doesn't need to look it up again
Name error variants after what went wrong, not what to do: `WrongPassword`, not `ShowError`
common_mistakes: Using `==` to compare `LoginResult` values directly — use `match` instead, it's clearer
Forgetting to handle all three variants after calling `try_login` — you might miss the error cases
